question: The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants was adopted at a Conference of Plenipotentiaries in which year?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2001**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs)** was adopted in **2001** at a Conference of Plenipotentiaries held in Stockholm, Sweden.
 
• This **Convention** is a global treaty aimed at protecting human health and the environment from chemicals that persist in the environment, accumulate in living organisms, and pose risks to human health.
 
• It specifically targets chemicals that are toxic, resistant to environmental degradation, and can be transported across international boundaries. *Hence, the adoption year is correctly stated as 2001.*
 
• **Major objectives:** The Convention seeks to eliminate or restrict the production and use of persistent organic pollutants (POPs). It also aims at reducing releases of these pollutants into the environment.
 
• The Convention initially addressed 12 specific chemicals known as the "dirty dozen," including pesticides like DDT and industrial chemicals like PCBs. Over time, more chemicals have been added to the list. *Hence, the Convention's focus is highly significant.*
 
• **Implementation:** The Convention requires parties to develop national implementation plans and take measures to reduce or eliminate the release of POPs. It also promotes international cooperation and support for capacity building in developing countries.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 2001.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs):**

 
 
• **POPs** are chemical substances that persist in the environment, bioaccumulate through the food chain, and pose a risk to human health and ecosystems.
 
• They include **pesticides, industrial chemicals, and unintentional by-products** like dioxins and furans.
 
 
 
• **History of the Stockholm Convention:**
 
 
• The Convention was adopted in **2001** and came into force on **May 17, 2004**, following ratification by the required number of countries.
 
• It was initiated by the United Nations Environment Programme (**UNEP**) to address global concerns regarding toxic chemicals.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Convention:**
 
 
• It has contributed significantly to global environmental protection by reducing the production and use of harmful chemicals.
 
• The Convention also promotes sustainable practices and the use of safer alternatives.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of the Stockholm Convention:**

 
 
• The Convention targets **POPs** under three categories: **intentionally produced chemicals** (like pesticides and industrial chemicals), **unintentionally produced chemicals** (like dioxins), and those slated for elimination or restriction.
 
• It promotes the use of **best environmental practices (BEPs)** and **best available techniques (BATs)** to minimize releases of POPs.
 
 
 
• **Examples of POPs:**
 
 
• **DDT:** A pesticide banned in many countries due to its harmful effects on health and the environment.
 
• **PCBs:** Industrial chemicals used in electrical equipment, now restricted globally.
 
• **Dioxins:** Unintentionally produced during industrial processes; highly toxic.
